meta.title: Rubric — Governed AI operations
meta.description: Rubric turns an AI agent's work into a decision record: the evidence it used, the risk it found, who approved it, what ran, and what changed.

hero.title:
Every agent action,
on the record.
hero.lead: Rubric turns an agent's work into a decision you can inspect: the evidence it used, the risk it found, who approved it, what ran, and what changed.

record.label: Decision record
record.signalValue: Support volume up 38%, platform usage down 17%

demo.title: From a mention to a governed action
demo.lead: A teammate asks a question in a thread. The agent gathers evidence across tickets, usage, billing and CRM, scores the risk, routes an approval, executes, and writes the record. Two scenarios run in a loop: churn risk and silent migration.
demo.note: The demo interface is in English.

product.title: A decision object, not a chat log
product.lead: Most agents tell you what they did. Rubric keeps the structure that lets someone else check it.

items.title: Evidence, not vibes
items.body: Every claim links to the ticket, invoice, usage row or CRM field it came from. If the source is missing, the decision says so.

items.title: Risk with a threshold
items.body: The agent scores the decision against your policy and stops when confidence is not enough for the action it proposes.

items.title: Human gates
items.body: Approvals are explicit and role-scoped. Nothing executes until the right person accepts the proposed action.

items.title: Execution with receipts
items.body: Each step is a logged call: what ran, in what order, and what came back. Failures are part of the record, not hidden.

items.title: One audit trail
items.body: Input, evidence, risk, approval, execution and outcome share a single identifier you can replay later.

steps.title: Ask
steps.body: Someone asks a question where the work already happens. The agent resolves who is asking, for which account, and under which policy.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body: It queries the connected systems, grounds each claim, scores the risk and proposes an action with a confidence level.

steps.title: Attest
steps.body: A human approves or rejects. The action runs inside its scope and every step closes the record.

governance.title: Control is the product
governance.lead: Governance is not a settings page added at the end. It is the shape of every decision.

items.title: Approval before effect
items.body: High-risk decisions cannot execute without a named approver. The gate is recorded with the decision.

items.title: Scoped access
items.body: The agent reads with the narrowest credentials that answer the question, and writes only inside an approved action.

items.title: Replayable
items.body: The same inputs produce the same record, so an incident review does not depend on someone's memory of the thread.

items.title: Bounded actions
items.body: Each action declares its blast radius: what it touches, who it notifies, and what it will not do.

developers.title: A decision is an object you can inspect
developers.lead: The demo on this page models the same shape an integration would use: evidence in, risk assessed, approval requested, action executed, record closed.
points: Evidence and policy are explicit inputs, not prompt text.
Risk and confidence are returned as fields, not prose.
Approval and execution are separate, auditable steps.

footer.tagline: Rubric is a product concept and an open-source demo. The agent shown here is scripted; it is not connected to live systems.
